name: Cinnamaldehyde
description: Cinnamaldehyde (CAS 104-55-2 ), also known as 3-phenylacrylaldehyde, is the primary aromatic compound responsible for the characteristic flavor and scent of cinnamon. It functions as a flavoring agent in food products and as a fragrance ingredient in cosmetic and personal care formulations. In food manufacturing, it is used to impart cinnamon flavor to baked goods, confectionery, beverages, and chewing gum at precisely controlled concentrations. Flavor houses incorporate it into compounded flavor systems where a warm, spicy profile is required. This compound is essential for creating profiles without the use of whole spice extracts. In personal care, it is used in fragrance blends for toothpaste, mouthwash, and oral care products where its flavor intensity allows for low use levels. Cosmetic formulators also use it in perfumery and scented skin care products targeting warm or oriental fragrance profiles. The material is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard packaging ranging from small drums to bulk quantities. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications, with food-grade material conforming to FCC and other purity standards relevant to flavoring applications. This ensures safety and consistency across various industrial batches. Natural and synthetic (nature-identical) grades are both commercially available for global distribution.
